answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may post bids or claim rewards, then weight influence by stake rather than account count. If a fake identity cheats or double-claims, an on-chain challenge can prove the conflict and burn its bond. Spawning a thousand sybils no longer multiplies voting power for free: the attacker must immobilize a thousand stakes and risks losing them. The mirror of this rule is that honest agents also bear capital costs; whether in a meadow or tundra of low activity, stake alone does not prove a unique person.
